Vijaykumar A. Patil J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the State questioning the correctness of the judgment of acquittal dated 21.07.2018 passed by the VI Addl. District and Special Judge, Mysuru in S.C.No.64/2016.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts in brief leading to filing of this appeal are that on 17.11.2015 at about 10:00 a.m., while PW-1 was going by walk, accused No.1 came in a Tata Indica car belonging to PW-5 and asked PW-1 to sit in the car by threatening her.
Both alighted from the car at Yelawala bus stop and from there, in a KSRTC bus they went to Hassan.
In Hassan, accused No.1 married PW-1, a minor girl at Prasanna Ganapathi Temple.

The accused took PW-1 to NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB Mallapura Village of Belur Taluk and there they resided in the house of one Rajesh and informed him that they had recently married and come to see Belur and Halebeedu.
Accused and PW-1 stayed in Janatha House No.1 of Rajesh and on that night against the wish of PW-1, accused subjected her to forcible sexual intercourse.
On 19.11.2015, accused took her back to Mysuru and dropped her to Sub- urban bus stand and threatened her not to reveal the incident to her parents.
PW-1, victim girl went back to her house and revealed about the incident to her mother who lodged a complaint with the jurisdictional police.

The police registered the same in Crime No.109/2015 for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376, 506 of IPC and also Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'the POCSO Act').

sentences.text:
The investigating officer completed the investigation, filed charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 5(l)
read with Section 6 of POCSO Act, Section 363, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 9 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.
The accused pleaded not guilty.

The prosecution has examined 13 witnesses as PW-1 to PW-13,
got marked 22 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P22.
The respondent - accused did not adduce evidence.
The Trial Court, on appreciation of the evidence proceeded to acquit the accused of the charged offences.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment of acquittal, the State is in appeal.

sentences.text: Sri.Thejesh P., learned
High Court Government Pleader appearing for the appellant - State submits that the Trial Court has committed an error in appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record.
It is submitted that the prosecution has examined the victim who has clearly deposed that the accused abducted and took her to Hassan and forcefully married her.

Thereafter,
he forcibly took her to Mallapura Village and committed rape on her.

The Trial Court has committed grave error in giving a finding that the victim voluntarily went with the accused and married in the temple and further the prosecution failed to prove the age of NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB the victim.
The oral testimonies of 13 witnesses and 22 documents would clearly establish that the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.

It is further submitted that PW-1,
the minor victim girl and PW-2 the complainant and mother of the victim girl, have narrated the incident in their evidence which clearly establishes that the accused, taking advantage of the acquaintance had forcibly kidnapped PW-1, taken her to Belur, confined her in a house and had committed forcible sexual act against her will.
It is also submitted that the Trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidence of the medical officer who has opined that the hymen of victim girl was found torn.
PW-6, Principal of the college has stated that PW-1 is a minor as on the date of incident.
Hence, the prosecution has proved the case beyond all reasonable doubts.
He seeks to allow the appeal by reversing the judgment of acquittal and convicting the accused for the charged offences.
Sri . V.S.Vinayaka, learned Amicus Curiae appearing for the respondent No.2 - defacto complainant submits that the Trial Court has committed a grave error in acquitting the accused.
It is submitted that there are some minor contradictions in the evidence of PW-1 that cannot be the basis to acquit the accused of the charged offences.
It is submitted that PW-1 has clearly stated that against her will, she has been taken to Hassan then to Belur and the accused committed sexual act on her.
The accused had threatened PW-1 that she shall not disclose the incident to her parents.
These facts have not been properly appreciated by the Trial Court which resulted in acquittal of the accused.
He seeks to allow the appeal filed by the State by convicting the accused for the offences charged against him.
6. Per contra Sri.A.C.Chethan, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 supports the judgment of acquittal and submits that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

It is submitted that PW-1 is not consistent in her statement before the police, her statement NC:
2024:KHC:2297-DB recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate and before the Trial Court.

PW-1 admitted that she had acquaintance with the accused, further admitted that accused has not harmed her during her stay, she has not made any attempt to raise hue and cry nor made any attempt to run away from the spot which clearly establishes that PW-1 has voluntarily gone with the accused.

It is submitted that PW-1, in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. has not stated anything about sexual harassment or sexual intercourse by the accused which clearly establishes that the prosecution has falsely implicated the accused.
It is further submitted that the Trial Court has rightly recorded the finding that PW-1 who is a victim had 3 versions and there are lot of contradictions and omissions in her statement.
Hence, the evidence of PW-1 would not establish the guilt of the accused.

It is also submitted that PW-2 who is the mother of the victim,
reiterated the complaint averments. PW-3, PW-4, PW-5, PW- 7, PW-8 and PW-11 have not The State Of Karnataka vs Shivakumar on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43882041/
3 supported the case of the prosecution.

sentences.text: PW-9, medical officer, in her cross- NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB examination admitted that if the teenage girl is indulged in sports, there would be possibility of hymen being not intact.
It is contended that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubts.
The Trial Court, by a well considered judgment acquitted the accused by proper appreciation of evidence which does not call for any interference in the appeal.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

7. We have heard the learned High Court Government Pleader for the appellant - State, learned Amicus Curiae for the defacto complainant - respondent No.2, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and perused the entire evidence and the judgment of the Trial Court.

8. The story of the prosecution is that PW-1, minor girl was kidnapped by the accused from lawful guardianship, compelled her to marry him and forced to have illicit sexual intercourse by taking her to Mallapura Village.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB prosecution has examined PW-1, victim girl.
PW-1 stated that PW-2 is her mother and she studied PUC from Maharani Women's Junior College, Mysuru and her date of birth is 10.05.1998 as per her school records.
She stated that accused was working as driver in her house.
She further stated that she joined Mahajana Degree College.
On 17.11.2015, when she went to collect hall ticket for the I Semester exam of B.Com, accused was sitting in the car, he called her to sit in the car which she refused.
At that time, he threatened her and insisted her to board the car.
Then he took her to Yelawala bus stand and from there they boarded a bus to Hassan.
Thereafter they went to Belur and stayed in the house of a person known to accused.
There they stayed for two days and the accused committed forcible sexual intercourse on her.
Thereafter, on 19.11.2015 at about 6 a.m. they came to Mysuru, accused dropped her at Sub-urban bus stand, asked her to go home and not to reveal about the incident to her parents.
Accordingly, she went to her home and informed her mother about the incident.
The police recorded her statement and she was - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB examined by the doctor and also statement was recorded by the Magistrate.
In the cross-examination, PW-1 has admitted that she had acquaintance with the accused, they had met prior to the incident and she went along with the accused to Hassan and got married.
Thereafter, they went to Mallapura and stayed there.
She also admitted that she did not raise hue and cry nor made any attempt to run away from the company of accused.
In Section 164 statement recorded before the learned Magistrate, she admitted that she voluntarily went along with the accused.
The case of the prosecution is that the victim being a minor was abducted and sexual intercourse was done by the accused.
On close reading of the evidence of PW-1, it is evident that PW-1 voluntarily went along with the accused and consented for sexual intercourse.
9. PW-2 who is the mother of the victim, has reiterated the complaint averments in her evidence.
In the cross-examination, she has admitted that the accused was acquainted with their family.

PW-3 is a witness who has The State Of Karnataka vs Shivakumar on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43882041/
4 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB signed the spot mahazar where the alleged abduction has taken place.

sentences.text: He stated that he is ignorant about the contents of the mahazar.
PW-4 has not supported the case of prosecution.
PW-5, PW-8 and PW-11 are the persons who were alleged to have provided shelter to the accused and victim.
They have not supported the case of prosecution.
They have stated that they do not know the accused and the victim girl.

10. The prosecution has examined PW-6, the Principal of SBRR Mahajan First Grade College,
Mysuru who produced a letter indicating the date of birth of the victim as 10.05.1998 at Ex.P7.

entities.text:
SBRR Mahajan First Grade College,
Mysuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The prosecution, in order to prove that the victim was a minor, placed reliance on the aforesaid evidence.

On perusal of Ex.P7, which is a letter written by the Principal of the said College stating the date of birth of the victim as 10.05.1998, it is evident that if the said date of birth of the victim is taken into consideration, as on the date of alleged commission of crime, the victim was aged 17 years 6 months 9 days.
The document at Ex.P7 is not a - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB conclusive proof of evidence.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of cases has held that marginal benefit of 2 years on either side with regard to the age of the victim in the absence of any conclusive evidence on record may be given.
Hence, this Court is of the considered view that prosecution has failed to prove that the victim is minor.
Admittedly, the victim was studying B.Com, which further creates a doubt in the mind of the Court whether on the date of alleged commission of crime, the victim was minor or not.
11. The prosecution has examined PW-9 who is a medical officer and has examined the victim.
She has deposed that victim had informed her that she was in love with the accused and narrated the incident.
The said witness has stated that there were no injuries on the body of the victim girl including her private parts.
But, hymen was not intact.
In the cross-examination, it was elicited that due to sports activities there is a possibility of hymen being ruptured.
The evidence of PW-9 creates further doubt with - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB regard to the alleged abduction of victim by the accused and forceful sexual intercourse.
12. The Trial Court, on assessing the evidence of the prosecution has recorded a categorical finding that there are number of contradictions in the evidence of PW-1 and other witnesses.

The Trial Court has further recorded the finding that the prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was below 18 years of age as on the date of alleged offence as she is mature enough to take a decision.

The Trial Court has come to the conclusion that there was no threat or inducement by the accused while taking the victim to Hassan and thereafter, to Mallapura and there is no forceful sexual act on the part of the accused and proceeded to acquit the accused.

This Court, on re-appreciation of the The State Of Karnataka vs Shivakumar on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43882041/

sentences.text: entire evidence on record is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to prove that the victim PW-1 is a minor at the time of alleged commission of crime.
The prosecution has further failed to prove that the accused has abducted PW-1 and committed sexual act without her - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:2297-DB consent.
The Trial Court has recorded the categorical finding that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt and the benefit of doubt is given to the accused.
The said finding is neither perverse nor contrary to the evidence on record calling for interference in the acquittal judgment of the Trial Court.
13. For the aforementioned reasons, we do not find any merit in the appeal.
The same is hereby dismissed.
